figure.caption: GEPA proposes a new candidate in every iteration by improving existing candidates using one of the two strategies (Reflective Prompt Mutation (Section ~\ref{sec:reflective_prompt_mutation}) or System Aware Merge (Appendix ~\ref{sec:merge})), first evaluating them on a minibatch, and if improved, evaluating on a larger dataset. Instead of selecting the best performing candidate to mutate always, which can lead to a local-optimum, GEPA introduces Pareto-based candidate sampling (Section~\ref{sec:pareto_based_selection}), which filters and samples from the list of best candidates \textit{per} task, ensuring sufficient diversity. Overall, these design decisions allow GEPA to be highly sample-efficient while demonstrating strong generalization.
